result.summary:
Program B as stated is false, and the missing piece is now pinned down exactly. Main results:

(1) The structure behind absorption, found here. Every attractor of the driven right half for 0001, 0011 and 0111 is "ether segment + wall".
- The ether E is a spatio-temporally periodic rule-30 pattern with spatial period 7 and temporal period 4. Its columns are B1..B5, c, c = 0011, 0110, 1101, 0101, 0011, 0001, 0001.
- Up to a time shift, 0001, 0011, 0111 and 0101 are all ether columns.
- The wall W109 is a 109-state, 13-cell strip attached to the right of a B3 column. It is closed under every right input.
- This explains every observed zone width: 11, 12 (+7m) for 0001; 9, 10, 13 (+7m) for 0011; 8 (+7m) for 0111; 14 for 01.
- All 109/188/188 states of the round-1 traps S_w are ether+wall states with the smallest ether segment.

(2) Lean, file EtherWall.lean: 0 sorry, axioms propext and Quot.sound only, compiles in about 4.5 s. Checked kernel results:
- `ether_rule`: E is a rule-30 orbit.
- `wallOK_true`: the wall certificate holds.
- `trap_invariant`: holds for any rule-30 evolution on columns p ≥ 0.
- `ether_wall_trap` / `no_ether_wall_entry`: if c = w^∞ from T, the true right half never enters any member of the infinite family. A member is: columns 1..k equal to ether, with column k a B3, followed by a wall state, for any k in the residue class.
- `never_enters_S0001/S0011/S0111`: explicit finite right halves (ether columns + wall + white) driven by w^∞ never enter the round-1 traps. This refutes the literal claim.
- `Absorption` (a Prop) together with `absorption_excludes` and `least_period_four_of_absorption`: absorption into the family for all finite right halves would exclude all three words for every transient.

(3) No fixed-width trap can work. I extracted certificates in C and checked them with an independent Python simulator: a path plus two closed walks whose white-phase outputs do not commute. They show that no closed, output-eventually-periodic strip set of width ≤ 20 contains a pure-ether strip. Hence the ether(≥20) + wall + white configurations never enter any trap of width ≤ 20.

(4) Evidence for the open piece. Every finite right half with support in [1,12] (all phases) enters the family. So does the true right half at every T in [1, 300000] with c replaced by w^∞ (1.2M runs per word). Maximum entry delays are 1017 (0001), 1869 (0011) and 829 (0111). Ether depth k reaches 31, 23 and 28, so deep family members are genuinely needed.

(5) The right edge is not the mechanism.
- Entry happens before the edge can causally reach the boundary layer, whenever T ≥ ~2000.
- Entry is just as fast for effectively infinite random configurations and for spatially periodic ones.
- The "rigid right-edge structure" holds for every finite configuration: diagonals relative to the edge are purely periodic with 2-power periods. So it carries nothing beyond finite support.
- In the strip relaxation, trap-avoiding paths have essentially the full growth rate of all paths. So no strip-local ranking function exists.

(6) Period 2 behaves differently. 0101 is ether column B4, so the same trap family exists. Yet only about 3% of true right halves enter it, all within 118 steps; the rest never enter within 20000 steps. Absorption is therefore word-specific.

Missing piece: Absorption(w) — every finite right half driven by w^∞ eventually enters the ether+wall family. This is a claim about every orbit of a chaotic driven system, and I see no route to it from the edge, strips, or ranking.

(2) **Equivalent forms of Q_01.**

- Q_01 <=> BWR: for every depth d there is a bound B with a black cell of lam(alt f) in [d, d+B) for every f. This uses compactness, and the optimal B(d) is D(d) - d + 1.

(5) **Forced skeleton.** At a forced step, survival through the next forced step holds iff cells -2 and -3 differ. Column -2 is constant on forced pairs, column -3 is the complement of column -2 one step later, and columns -1 and -2 are never both white.

- Q_01 holds for every free-bit sequence with a p-periodic window [s0, s0+l] where 2l+2 > 2s0+m+4p, in particular every eventually periodic one.

The strategy as posed therefore cannot close Q_01. The remaining content is Mahler-type: the constrained side has positive entropy.

Backward determinism and the finite-preimage criterion.
(a) If zstep x = zstep y and x 0 = y 0, then x = y. At every forced step the earlier row is therefore determined by the later one.
(b) A history is determined by its row at time T and its wall column at times < T.
(c) The preimage of y with wall cell b is back b y. If y is white from index n >= 1, then back b y is finite iff back b y (n-1) = back b y n = false; otherwise every cell beyond n is black.

(a) Left permutivity gives x(i+1) = zstep x i xor (x i || rn x i). Induct on i with the pair (x i, x(i+1)), using rn x (j+1) = x j.
(b) Apply (a) at times T-1, T-2, ..., 0, using zorb_succ.
(c) zstep(back b y) = y by xor cancellation, and (a) gives uniqueness. For i >= n we have y i = 0, so back(i+1) = back(i) || back(i-1). If the pair at (n-1, n) is (0,0), zeros propagate by induction. Otherwise back(n+1) = 1, and by induction every later cell is 1, which contradicts finiteness.

claims.statement:
Locality and the edge-region barrier.
(a) Light cone: rows agreeing on [0,m) agree at time t on [0, m-t).
(b) Pivot: rows agreeing on [0,t) and differing at t differ at the wall at time t.
(c) Zero-run localization: a row that is white on [d, d+L) has the same wall column as its truncation to [0,d) for t < d+L.
(d) Far light cone: rows agreeing on [d,inf) agree at time t on [d+t, inf). In particular the left-edge region of width m-d (all of its left diagonals, at all times) depends only on the far part.
(e) Near-wall completion and edge-region barrier: for every far part z, every target column c and every d, some x equals z on [d,inf), has wall column c on [0,d), and has exactly the evolution of z on [d+t, inf) at every time t.

Q_01 is NOT proved. No monovariant of the requested kind exists among local quantities, and I prove that as a barrier theorem. I did find exact structure, and I proved it in Lean.

(1) Reformulation. The infinite constrained histories are exactly S = Theta({0,1}^N). Theta is the triangular map from the free bits f to the initial row, built by left-permutive reconstruction from columns 0 and 1. It is a homeomorphism with Z^2 Theta = Theta sigma, so S is a Cantor set: uncountable, not just the stripe. Q_01 says Theta(f) is never finitely supported.

(2) Epoch structure (Lean). The first deviation from ...10101 moves exactly one cell toward the wall per step. So in a surviving history, at time t it lies at a depth d with t + d even. The free bit f_s is 0 exactly when that deviation is at depth 2 (a reset). At a reset the row is 0,1,s_3..s_d and deviates again at depth d+1, where d is the next epoch length. A history dies exactly when an epoch has odd length. Near the wall the spacetime is a staircase of pure-stripe triangles whose hypotenuses lie on even anti-diagonals. (3) The stripe background has a genuine monovariant (Lean). If a row equals the stripe from depth L on, then Z^2 of it does too, so the last deviation never moves outward. claims.statement: Truncated stripes: let z_s(t,k) be the ZBL (depth k ≥ 1, wall at depth 0, z(t+1,k)=z(t,k+1) xor (z(t,k) or z(t,k-1))). For odd n, the start trunc_n (black exactly at odd depths ≤ n) has depth 1 black at every time t ≤ n and white at time n+1, which is even. So constrained runs from finite starts have unbounded length; the run from trunc_n lives exactly through time n.
claims.proof:
The infinite stripe S (black at odd depths) is a ZBL fixed point. For k ≥ 1, one of S(k), S(k-1) is black (S(0) = 0 is the wall), so the update gives ¬S(k+1) = S(k). trunc_n agrees with S on depths ≤ n+1 (n+1 is even, so white in S).
(i) By induction on t, z(t,k) = S(k) whenever k+t ≤ n+1: all three inputs (t-1,k+1), (t-1,k), (t-1,k-1) lie in that region, and S is fixed.
(ii) By induction, z(t,k) = ¬S(k) on the anti-diagonal k+t = n+2 (k ≥ 1). At t=0, depth n+2 is white in trunc_n and black in S. In the step, the xor input (t-1,k+1) lies on the same anti-diagonal and equals ¬S(k+1), while the or-inputs lie in region (i). Hence z = ¬(S(k+1) xor (S(k) or S(k-1))) = ¬S(k).
Conclusion: depth 1 equals S(1) = 1 for t ≤ n and ¬S(1) = 0 at t = n+1.

Exact structure of the wall frame.
(a) Let Φ map the depth-1 sequence y to the initial configuration it forces (left-permutive reconstruction, wall = 0). Φ is a homeomorphism of {0,1}^N and is triangular: x_0(depth k) = y_{k-1} xor H_k(y_0..y_{k-2}).
(b) Let Y = {y : y_{2s} = 1}. Then Ψ(f) := Φ(1,f_0,1,f_1,...) is a homeomorphism {0,1}^N → Φ(Y), and it conjugates the shift on f to the double step G. Q_01 is equivalent to: Ψ(f) is never eventually zero. Equivalently, the remaining life of a finite x (its Φ(Y)-compatibility depth) is always finite.
(c) Wall-frame abstraction of width w (window = depths 1..w, free input at depth w+1, constraint at even times). Its greatest fixed point, the set of states with an infinite constrained abstract run, is exactly Pref_w(Φ(Y)), which has 2^⌊w/2⌋ elements.
(d) For eventually periodic f, Ψ(f) is spatially eventually periodic. Examples: f=(10)^∞ gives period 7, f=(110)^∞ gives 84, f=(11010)^∞ gives 155.

(a) Left-permutivity gives x_t(p-1) = x_{t+1}(p) xor (x_t(p) or x_t(p+1)). So column -1 plus the wall determine every column. The pivot y_{k-1} enters x_0(-k) by xor, which makes Φ triangular and bijective; both Φ and its inverse are continuous.
(b) Fix y_even = 1 and parametrise the free odd entries by f. Shifting y by 2 is the same as advancing two time steps.
(c) An infinite abstract run with inputs v_t fixes columns -1 through -(w+1) for all times. Reconstruct leftwards using the equation in (a). That equation is exactly rule 30 at the reconstructed cell, so the resulting infinite configuration's ZBL run realises the abstract run, and it lies in Φ(Y). The converse inclusion is immediate. The count follows from (a): x_0[1..w] corresponds bijectively to y_0..y_{w-1} with the even entries fixed.

Case 1, the cycle accepts somewhere: then ρ ≥ |Z_j| + 2k - 2π = n + 2j - 2π. But the decreases from time 0 give ρ ≤ n - j, so 3j ≤ 2π.
Case 2, the cycle never accepts: then ρ ≤ 4j + 2·2^N. But the remaining life gives ρ ≥ (n-1)/2 - j - 1.

Why each approach failed:

1. WALL FRAME (window of any width w, free input). Its states with infinite constrained runs are exactly Pref_w(Φ(Y)), all 2^⌊w/2⌋ windows (A3). Every window of a finite configuration is also a window of an infinite surviving configuration: the stripe, Ψ(f), and the 7-periodic c7. The abstraction cannot see finiteness. Strip relaxations on both sides fail for the same reason (c7, A5).

2. EDGE FRAME. Here the system is exact and autonomous (one-way: relative cell r depends only on r-2, r-1, r). But the constraint sits at relative position W+t-1, which leaves every bounded window. All abstract runs are infinite and the constraint is invisible.

3. WALL + EDGE WITH A SUMMARISED MIDDLE.
- Any finite summary fails by B1 (A2).
- Adding the width as a counter fails by B2 (A4, two-sided A5). Truncated stripes have a constant wall window, an edge window that does not depend on n and is eventually periodic, and a life of about n. That forces R(M+2P, S, E) ≤ R(M, S, E) - P for all large M.

4. k-INDUCTION, IC3/PDR, BDDs. On any finite abstraction these return lassos (B1). For fixed width the problem is bounded model checking, done exhaustively for W ≤ 55 (A10). Nothing generalises across W. z3's Spacer/PDR was not run, because every abstraction it could check has a lasso.

5. ADDITIVE (PATTERN-COUNT) LYAPUNOV FUNCTIONS. Excluded by A7: balance of rule 30 plus no nontrivial conservation laws of rule 30² (ordinary to range 12, alternating to range 10). Not excluded: nonlinear functions of pattern counts, and densities of larger range or position period above 2.

6. DFA PREFIX RANKINGS.
- Reading from the edge: impossible for every size (A6, Lean).
- Reading from the wall: none with ≤ 6 states (A8). The 7-state instance timed out. Truncated stripes cannot kill these, because a wall-reading automaton can measure the stripe length.

7. RENORMALISATION / SIMPLE STRUCTURE OF Ψ. The ANF of x_0(-k) in the free bits has degree growing like k/2 and ever more monomials. No self-similar block map was found. The longest survivors (A10) begin by following Ψ(0^∞) = 1(10)^∞ and then look random.

8. DEVIATION-FRONT FRAME. This is the only frame with an exact finite abstraction, and only near time-periodic surviving backgrounds (A9, A12).
- The certificate grows fast with the tail length: maximum post-arrival survival 31 → 45 → ≥ 62, and front-window orbits 8192 → 5·10^8 → more than 10^9.
- A generic finite configuration is a truncation of an aperiodic Φ(Y)-element. Ahead of its front the background is then aperiodic, so the front frame is driven non-autonomously and has no finite abstraction.

Bottom line: every local, finite-state, additive or edge-automatic invariant is excluded. A proof of Q_01, or of the two-sided period-2 problem over all finite configurations, must use non-local information equivalent to the Φ(Y)-compatibility depth.
